facts.statement: The genus contains a single species, Herugavialis cairensis, found near Cairo, Egypt.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Herugavialis cairensis, known from near Cairo, Egypt.

facts.statement: Herugavialis lacked a maxilla process within its lacrimal gland, a feature present in all living crocodilians.
facts.quote: Herugavialis did not have a maxilla process within its lacrimal gland, whereas all extant (living) crocodilians do.

facts.statement: The species was moved to the new genus Herugavialis in a 2026 study.
facts.quote: In a 2026 study, it was moved to its own genus, Herugavialis.

facts.statement: Herugavialis is classified as a member of Gavialoidea.
The table lists the age as Middle Miocene, though other sources specify Eocene.
The fossil range of Herugavialis is the Eocene, specifically the Lutetian stage.
The type locality is the Mokattam Formation.
The fossil was found in Egypt.
CT scans revealed numerous anatomical differences between Herugavialis and contemporaneous Egyptian species like Eogavialis africanum and Paratomistoma courti.
Herugavialis cairensis is diagnosed by characteristics including telescoped orbits.
It is debated whether the decline in Mediterranean gavialoid diversity was driven by habitat reduction due to global cooling and declining sea levels.
It is debated whether Miocene warming facilitated a rebound in diversity before Late Miocene extirpation caused by the Messinian Salinity Crisis.
